backgrounds: Essentially a single set: a coastal city waterfront promenade/boardwalk lined with a metal guardrail, overlooking a harbor. In the opening seconds the scene is a wide shot of a crowd running in panic down a multi-lane road along the water, with a dense high-rise skyline (skyscrapers, office towers) behind them and a massive tsunami wave looming on the horizon. The video then settles into one static two-shot location: the same promenade railing with the giant wave frozen/slowly looming in the background for the rest of the runtime, where the two main characters have their conversation. Sky is overcast and grey throughout. Opening and closing include flat black title/outro cards with text.
props: giant tsunami wave (background threat, spans full width of frame)
metal pedestrian guardrail/railing along the promenade
abandoned cars parked/crashed along the street (sedan, hatchback, several parked cars)
ornate black lamp posts (street lamps) lining the road
scattered loose papers and litter blown across the pavement
debris (cans, bottles, shoes) strewn on the ground
distant birds/small dark shapes flying in the sky
yellow 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' ticket-style graphic on outro card
lighting_notes: Overcast, diffuse grey daylight with a cool, desaturated color grade; no strong directional shadows. Flat, even lighting on the stop-motion figures keeps focus on facial expressions rather than dramatic light/shadow play, consistent with a disaster/apocalypse mood.
color_palette: muted teal/blue-green (the tsunami wave and harbor water)
black (character coat, outro background, lamp posts)
bright yellow (title text and outro badge, single vivid accent color)
visual_complexity_notes: The scene starts as a busier, detailed wide shot (crowd of running background characters, city skyline, cars, litter) but quickly narrows to a minimal two-character close-up against a static, repeated wave backdrop for almost the entire video. This shift from dense chaos to a simple, locked composition seems deliberate: it establishes stakes visually up front, then removes distraction so all attention goes to the two characters' deadpan dialogue and expressions.
